title: Max flow, min cut, bipartite matching
relevance: Medium — “assign people↔jobs / seats↔students” bipartite matching is the interview slice; raw Dinic / min-cut / MCMF is mostly Candidate-Master rating stretch Striver never covers.
company_notes: Boy–girl / worker–job pairs under compatibility → bipartite matching (School Dance / Tessoku A69). Assign each employee exactly one task minimizing total cost → assignment / Hungarian / MCMF (CSES Task Assignment). Seat students so no two can cheat / cover coins by deleting rows or columns → independent set / vertex cover via bipartite matching + König (Coin Grid; LC-style classroom seating). Minimum walls/cells to block all paths from A to B → min cut (Police Chase / Treasure Island), often “cut the network / remove fewest roads.”

phases.goal: Map assignment, compatibility, blockers, and threshold-check wording to bipartite matching / flow / min-cut rather than forcing raw Dinic.

must_hit.point: Interview slice is “assign people↔jobs / seats↔students” bipartite matching; raw Dinic / min-cut / MCMF is mostly Candidate-Master stretch Striver never covers.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names people↔jobs / seats↔students matching as the OA ask and treats full Dinic/min-cut/MCMF as stretch.

must_hit.point: Spot signals: assignment, pairwise compatibility, edge/vertex-disjoint paths, “minimum blockers,” or “binary-search a threshold then check a matching/flow.”
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists those statement cues and reaches for matching/flow/min-cut.

must_hit.point: Boy–girl / worker–job under compatibility → bipartite matching; employee↔task minimizing cost → Hungarian / MCMF; seat/cheat or clear coins by rows/cols → König vertex cover; block all paths A→B → min cut.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps each OA wording to matching, assignment, König, or min-cut.

must_hit.point: Grid tiling / checkerboard 1×2 tiles and node-split “use ≤1” models are flow/matching stretch beyond the basic interview slice.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions checkerboard bipartition + 1×2 tiles or vertex split as advanced modeling.

probes: Is this worker–job pairing, cost assignment, row/col cover, or blocking paths—and which model does that force?
What wording makes you binary-search a threshold and then check a matching or flow?

hints.1: Ask whether the ask is pairs under compatibility, one-task cost assignment, delete rows/cols, or cut all s–t paths.
hints.2: Compatibility pairs → s→L→R→t matching; cost assignment → Hungarian/MCMF; rows/cols clear → König; block paths → min cut; threshold then feasible → BS+matching/flow.
hints.3: Say: interview slice is people↔jobs / seats↔students matching; signals are assignment, compatibility, disjoint paths, minimum blockers, BS+matching/flow; worker–job → School Dance/A69; cost → Task Assignment; cheat/coins → Coin Grid König; walls/roads → Police Chase/Treasure Island min cut.

phases.goal: State the flow network or unit bipartite model, min-cut recovery, and when BS+matching or node-split applies.

must_hit.point: Build a directed network with capacities; max flow is maximum “stuff” from s to t under capacity + conservation (Edmonds–Karp / Dinic); by max-flow min-cut that equals the cheapest edge set disconnecting s from t.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States capacity+conservation max flow and equates it to min cut.

must_hit.point: Bipartite matching is the unit-capacity special case s → L (cap 1) → R (cap 1) → t; flow equals matching size.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Draws s→L→R→t with caps 1 and equates flow to matching size.

must_hit.point: Recover the cut: nodes reachable from s in the residual graph; cut edges are u→v with u reachable and v not.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes residual reachability from s and the reachable/unreachable cut edges.

must_hit.point: Binary search + matching/flow: monotone “can we achieve threshold x?” → rebuild caps / keep edges ≥ x → check flow/matching.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States BS on x, filter/rebuild by threshold, then matching/flow feasibility.

must_hit.point: Edge-disjoint paths = unit-capacity max flow; node capacity c(v) → split v_in → v_out with cap c(v), in-edges to v_in, out-edges from v_out.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names unit-cap path packing and the vin/vout split for vertex caps.

probes: How do you turn bipartite matching into a flow network?
After max flow, how do you recover the min-cut edges?
When do you binary-search a threshold before running matching or flow?

hints.1: Think source/sink caps for left/right, residual reachability for the cut, and monotone feasibility for BS.
hints.2: Matching → s→L→R→t caps 1; cut → residual BFS/DFS from s; BS → keep edges ≥ x then check; disjoint paths → unit caps; vertex cap → vin→vout.
hints.3: Say: max flow under capacity+conservation equals min cut; bipartite is s→L(cap 1)→R(cap 1)→t; cut = residual-reachable u to unreachable v; BS threshold x then rebuild/check; unit-cap flow for edge-disjoint paths; split v_in→v_out for c(v).

phases.goal: Code Dinic/Edmonds–Karp residuals, matching reconstruction, cut listing, and node-split / path decomposition.

must_hit.point: Dinic (or Edmonds–Karp) from memory: level graph + blocking flow; use long long for capacities/flow.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names level graph + blocking flow and long long capacities/flow.

must_hit.point: Residual edges: every forward edge has a reverse with capacity 0; augmenting path updates both.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Adds reverse edges at capacity 0 and updates both directions on augment.

must_hit.point: Matching edges are L→R with flow 1; reconstruct pairs from those saturated matching edges (School Dance).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Walks L→R edges carrying flow 1 to list the matching.

must_hit.point: After max flow, residual BFS/DFS from s lists min-cut edges u→v with u reachable, v not (Police Chase).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Runs residual search from s and emits cut edges across the frontier.

must_hit.point: König: max matching = min vertex cover; recover the cover from the min-cut of the matching network (Coin Grid).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States König equality and recovers cover via the matching-network min-cut.

must_hit.point: Decompose edge-disjoint paths by walking saturated edges and subtracting; assignment with costs → MCMF or Hungarian (CSES Task Assignment).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes saturated-edge path walking/subtract and names Hungarian/MCMF for costs.

probes: Walk me through residual reverse edges and one augment.
How do you reconstruct the bipartite matching or the min-cut edge list?
How do you enforce a vertex capacity in the network?

hints.1: Template first (levels/blocking flow), then reverses, then what you read off after the flow.
hints.2: long long + reverse cap 0; matching = L→R flow 1; cut = residual s-reach frontier; vin→vout for node caps; saturated walk for path pack; König from matching cut.
hints.3: Say: Dinic level graph + blocking flow with long long; reverse edges capacity 0, update both; matching edges L→R flow 1; residual BFS/DFS from s for cut; König cover from matching-network min-cut; decompose saturated edges; costs → MCMF/Hungarian.

phases.goal: State Dinic’s bipartite unit-matching bound and when Hungarian beats general MCMF.

must_hit.point: Dinic on the unit-capacity bipartite matching network is O(E√V) (Hopcroft–Karp complexity).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Quotes O(E√V) for Dinic on s→L→R→t unit caps.

must_hit.point: Assignment with costs: Hungarian for dense n≤200, otherwise min-cost max-flow; CSES Task Assignment is the template.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Picks Hungarian when dense n≤200, else MCMF, citing Task Assignment.

must_hit.point: Don’t force flow when n is small: matching-shaped OA tasks may be assignment DP (Armchairs / Chef Monocarp).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Switches to assignment DP on small n instead of building a flow network.

probes: What is Dinic’s complexity on unit bipartite matching?
When do you prefer Hungarian over MCMF for assignment?

hints.1: Separate the special bipartite unit-cap bound from the dense assignment algorithm choice.
hints.2: Unit bipartite Dinic → O(E√V); dense n≤200 costs → Hungarian; else MCMF; tiny n → maybe assignment DP.
hints.3: Say: Dinic on s→L→R→t caps 1 is O(E√V) (Hopcroft–Karp complexity); Hungarian for dense n≤200 else MCMF (Task Assignment); small-n matching-shaped OAs → Armchairs/Chef Monocarp DP.

phases.goal: Catch residual bugs, wrong cut/matching readout, skipped node splits, and forcing flow on DP-sized OAs.

must_hit.point: Forcing a flow network on matching-shaped OAs when n is small — use assignment DP instead (Armchairs / Chef Monocarp).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Refuses unnecessary Dinic and names assignment DP on small n.

must_hit.point: Omitting reverse residual edges at capacity 0 (or updating only the forward edge) breaks augmentation.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Requires reverse cap-0 edges and paired updates on every augment.

must_hit.point: Listing “min cut” edges without residual BFS/DFS from s after max flow (reachable u, unreachable v).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Insists on residual reachability from s before emitting cut edges.

must_hit.point: Putting a vertex capacity on v without splitting into v_in → v_out with cap c(v).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Corrects to vin→vout split with in-edges to vin and out-edges from vout.

must_hit.point: Forgetting that bipartite matching edges to report are L→R with flow 1 (not only s→L / R→t).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Reads the matching from L→R edges carrying flow 1.

probes: What breaks if you skip reverse residual edges?
How do people mis-recover the min cut or the matching pairs?
When is building Dinic the wrong first move on an “assignment” OA?

hints.1: Check residuals, what you read after flow, node-cap modeling, and whether n suggests DP.
hints.2: Always add reverse cap 0; cut only via residual s-reach; matching = L→R flow 1; vertex caps need vin→vout; small n → assignment DP.
hints.3: Say: don’t force flow when Armchairs/Chef Monocarp DP fits; reverse edges capacity 0 and update both; cut = residual reachable u to unreachable v; node cap → v_in→v_out cap c(v); report L→R flow 1 matching edges.

tradeoffs.topic: Bipartite unit flow (Dinic) vs assignment DP
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Seat/student or worker/job compatibility → s→L→R→t unit flow / Dinic. Many matching-shaped OAs with small n are assignment DP instead (Armchairs / Chef Monocarp)—don’t force flow.

tradeoffs.topic: Hungarian vs min-cost max-flow for assignment
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Assign each employee exactly one task minimizing total cost → Hungarian for dense n≤200, otherwise MCMF; CSES Task Assignment is the template.

tradeoffs.topic: Max-flow value vs min-cut edge recovery
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Max-flow min-cut equates the flow value to the cheapest disconnecting edge set; to list edges (Police Chase / Treasure Island blockers), run residual BFS/DFS from s and take u→v with u reachable, v not.

tradeoffs.topic: Max matching vs König min vertex cover
tradeoffs.strong_answer: In bipartite graphs max matching = min vertex cover; recover the cover from the min-cut of the matching network (CSES Coin Grid: rows↔cols to clear).

tradeoffs.topic: Plain threshold matching vs BS + shortest + matching / MCMF path pack
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Valuable Paper-style: binary-search edge-weight threshold then perfect matching. Stretch adds shortest-path travel limits before matching (Exploration plan) or MCMF to send exactly k edge-disjoint routes at min total length (Distinct Routes II / Parcel Delivery).

gotchas.trap: Reaching for Dinic on every “matching-shaped” OA.
gotchas.correction: When n is small, many are assignment DP (Armchairs / Chef Monocarp); don’t force flow.

gotchas.trap: Building residual graph without reverse edges at capacity 0, or updating only the forward edge on augment.
gotchas.correction: Every forward edge has a reverse with capacity 0; an augmenting path updates both.

gotchas.trap: Claiming min-cut edges without a residual search from s.
gotchas.correction: After max flow, BFS/DFS from s in the residual; cut edges are u→v with u reachable and v not.

gotchas.trap: Enforcing “vertex used at most c(v) times” by writing a capacity on v without splitting.
gotchas.correction: Split v_in → v_out with cap c(v); all in-edges go to v_in, out-edges leave v_out.

gotchas.trap: Reconstructing a bipartite matching from s→L or R→t only.
gotchas.correction: Matching edges are L→R with flow 1 (School Dance).

gotchas.trap: Treating row/col deletion or classroom non-cheating as a raw max-flow value only.
gotchas.correction: Use bipartite matching + König: max matching = min vertex cover, recover cover from the matching-network min-cut (Coin Grid).
